tasks.old_behavior: grub_cryptodisk_open() used grub_strcasecmp() to compare the user-provided UUID string (from 'cryptouuid/...' device name) against dev->uuid. Both the user input and the stored dev->uuid were dash-free (LUKS/LUKS2 stripped dashes before storing). Only exact dash-free UUID strings would match.
tasks.new_behavior: grub_cryptodisk_open() now uses grub_uuidcasecmp() which ignores dashes in both the user-provided UUID string and dev->uuid during comparison. dev->uuid now stores the raw header UUID (may contain dashes) for LUKS/LUKS2 devices. Users can specify UUIDs with or without dashes; both forms will match the same device.
tasks.compatibility_reason: This change relaxes the input contract for the cryptouuid/<UUID> device name. Previously, users had to provide dash-free UUIDs (e.g., '12345678123412341234123456789abc') for the device lookup to work. Now users can use the standard UUID format with dashes (e.g., '12345678-1234-1234-1234-123456789abc'), which matches what cryptsetup shows. This is backward-compatible because existing configurations using dash-free UUIDs continue to work. However, it is a config-visible behavior change that alters the accepted input format, and any scripts or automated tools that generate GRUB configurations may need to be aware of the new acceptance range.
tasks.test_recommendation: Test that 'cryptouuid/<UUID-with-dashes>' correctly opens LUKS1, LUKS2, and GELI encrypted devices. Verify that 'cryptouuid/<UUID-without-dashes>' continues to work (backward compatibility). Test with mixed dash patterns.

tasks.old_behavior: Each crypto backend module (GELI, LUKS, LUKS2) independently implemented UUID matching for the 'cryptomount -u <UUID>' command. GELI used grub_strcasecmp against generated UUID. LUKS and LUKS2 first stripped dashes from the header UUID using manual loops, then used grub_strcasecmp against the dash-stripped result. Users had to provide dash-free UUIDs to the -u option.
tasks.new_behavior: All crypto backends now use the centralized grub_uuidcasecmp() function for UUID matching. Dashes are no longer manually stripped; the comparison function itself ignores dashes. Users can now provide UUIDs with or without dashes to 'cryptomount -u'.
tasks.compatibility_reason: The 'cryptomount -u' CLI option now accepts dashed UUIDs in addition to dash-free UUIDs. Previously, users copying a UUID from cryptsetup output (which includes dashes) would get a non-match. Now those UUIDs work directly. This is backward-compatible: existing scripts using dash-free UUIDs continue to work. However, this is a CLI-visible behavior change that affects the accepted parameter format for a commonly used GRUB command.
tasks.test_recommendation: Test cryptomount -u with UUIDs containing dashes (standard format), without dashes, and with irregular dash placement. Test with GELI, LUKS1, and LUKS2 encrypted volumes. Verify correct device selection with multiple encrypted volumes.
